note: Windows has only four resize cursors, so all eight one-way values draw as two-headed arrows there. Other systems and Linux themes may draw true one-way arrows. Prefer ew, ns, nesw and nwse.
The two-way arrows are native nearly everywhere. col-resize and row-resize look like split bars on some systems and like plain two-way arrows on others.
Windows draws wait as a spinning ring and progress as an arrow with a small ring. Some systems draw them almost the same, so always show busy state in the interface too.
Often drawn by the browser rather than the OS, so the hand can look different in Chrome, Firefox and Safari on the same machine.
Where the OS has no native version, the browser ships its own image. Expect small differences between browsers, and occasionally a plain arrow.
Often the same circle-with-slash symbol. Don’t rely on the difference between them to carry meaning.
Chrome and Firefox ignore images larger than 128 × 128 px and use the fallback. 32 × 32 is the reliable size, and SVG files need a fixed width and height.
Every value comes from the desktop’s cursor theme, so the whole set can change when someone switches themes.
Phones and tablets draw no cursor. Anything a cursor communicates must also be visible in the interface.
